Plonix documentation

How to use Plonix, tool by tool: capture traffic, explore it, experiment on the Bench, prove what you find, and work with Claude. Plus how Plonix keeps your data and updates on your terms.

New to Plonix? Start with Getting started, or open the demo project from the Start screen and take the tour. The plonix command explains itself too: run plonix --help.

Your data

  • UpdatesPlonix.app never installs anything on its own. Every step that changes the app on disk is the user's choice, and closing a dialog always means "no".
  • Privacy and usage statisticsPlonix keeps your work on your computer. Captured traffic, projects, findings, scope and settings are stored only in folders on your disk (~/.plonix and your project folders).…
  • Crash reportsIf Plonix crashes, it writes a report on your computer and sends nothing. There is no crash-reporting service: you decide whether a report goes anywhere, and you see it first.
  • Code signing policyThe Windows installer, Plonix-Windows-setup.exe, is code-signed so Windows can show who published it and that it was not changed after it was built.
